messages:
Maya: Heads-up — SRE flagged a bug: a Viewer account was able to EDIT API keys in the Console. Repro steps attached, blocking for any sensitive key ops.

Derek: Who caught this and how soon can we repro?

Maya: @derek repro done with a fresh viewer user (incognito). Steps: Console -> Settings -> API keys -> edit name -> save. Changes accepted, no 403. Screenshot + HAR in the ticket.

Irene: that's bad. Does the audit log show the actor for the edit?

Maya: Audit entry exists but actor shows as "system" and role_inferred=viewer. Payload: `{"event":"api_key.update","actor":"system","target":"key-****","changes":{"name":"test"}}`. No user_id.

Sam: Could be role mapping change from last week's RBAC refactor. Any recent PR touching role_matrix.json or console-perm-gating?

Alex: I raised #4291 last week — split editor permissions by resource type. I did not touch api_keys mapping explicitly. I'll diff the release.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for release v1.58.3 by @alex (12:02 UTC).

Derek: Pause the canary immediately. We need to prevent further writes. @deploy-bot can you hold the rest of rollout?

deploy-bot: Canary paused. Remaining rollout blocked.

Irene: Immediate mitigation: create emergency policy to deny `api_keys.update` for role viewer in the policy service and apply. Who can push that now?

Alex: I can push a policy override to prod within 10m. Will add a conditional kill-switch on the feature flag too.

Maya: Also: KMS logs show key material access, but there is no corresponding audit event linking the console edit to a user. KMS access looks normal. Suspecting the UI permission gating allowed the action but the backend auth middleware escalated actor to system for reconciliation.

Derek: Action plan: 1) emergency deny for viewers on api_keys.update (Alex) 2) revert last RBAC matrix PR to canary branch (Irene) 3) add missing actor context to audit pipeline (Sam) 4) run user-level repro tests and add coverage (Maya).

Sam: I'll look at the audit pipeline — likely the event producer lost the request context when we switched to async worker for API key writes. That can drop headers. Quick check: `events.producer.send({event, ctx: request.ctx})` — if ctx undefined it becomes system.

Alex: Pushing policy override now. Patch: `PATCH /policies/emergency` body: {"role":"viewer","deny":["api_keys.update"]} (applied).

Maya: Confirmed: demo viewer cannot edit after policy override. 403 now.

Irene: Revert PR queued for canary branch. Rolling back RBAC matrix change that touched `console:api_keys` mapping.

Derek: Sam — can you instrument audit producer to include `user_id` and `request_id` in events and ship a hotfix? We need durable audit logs for compliance.

Sam: On it. Hotfix branch created. Will add tests and a check to make audit events fail loudly if ctx missing.

Alex: Note: KMS integration question — if actor is system, KMS logs still show client using HSM via service account. We should rotate any affected keys after we confirm blast radius. Thoughts?

Maya: I recommend rotation for keys edited in the last 24h and an integrity scan of all key metadata. Notify product owners.

Irene: I'll compile list of affected key IDs from DB — run SQL: `SELECT id, updated_at, updated_by FROM api_keys WHERE updated_at > now() - interval '24 hours'`.

Derek: Good. Also escalate to Compliance: missing actor in audit is a control failure. Prep an incident bridge for pager duty if scope > 1 customer.

Maya: Preliminary scope: 4 internal keys, 2 customer-managed keys touched. Irene to confirm.

Sam: Hotfix for audit producer pushed to prod (small rollout). It now throws an error and rejects write if request context missing. Monitoring set.

deploy-bot: Release v1.58.3 patch-audit hotfix deployed to prod (12:47 UTC).

Alex: Revert PR rolled back from canary and flagged for follow-up review.

Irene: Affected keys list: key-9912 (internal), key-4302 (customer: acme-corp). I'll open rotation tickets.

Maya: For postmortem: root cause appears to be async worker path for api key updates that omitted request context propagation during RBAC refactor. Contributing factors: no negative test for unauthorized update, audit producer didn't assert ctx presence, and canary lacked a focused auth test.

Derek: Follow-ups (owners): - Incident postmortem (Maya) - Audit producer assert + tests (Sam) - RBAC matrix unit tests + rollback safeguards (Alex) - Key rotations + cust communication (Irene) - Add end-to-end canary auth tests (Derek)

Maya: ETA for postmortem draft EOD. Will include timeline + diffs + remediation.

Irene: Notifying legal & compliance. I'll add customers in the communication channel once rotations confirmed.

Sam: Added CI guard: any async path must `propagate_ctx()` or CI fails. Will PR today.

Alex: Long-term: consider adding automated permission smoke tests in the canary gating flow for sensitive resource types (api_keys, kms_ops).

Maya: Agree. Thanks team. Keeping the thread updated as we progress. :white_check_mark:
